newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Monday with short-position holders covering their positions after buying heavily when prices were falling last week, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,460 ($2,828) yuan per tonne, up 30 yuan from 23,430 yuan.
It opened at an intra-day low of 23,400 yuan and hit a high of 23,510 a few minutes before closing.
June was unchanged at 22,770. July rose 60 to 23,000, August 50 to 23,200, October 70 to 23,530 and November 60 to 23,510.
Combined volume fell sharply to 18,000 tonnes from 39,780.
"The contracts went up today on short-covering," said one trader. "But the rise did not change poor market fundamentals much and the contracts are likely to fall on Tuesday."
"The key September contract ended below the 23,500-yuan resistance level, indicating market sentiment did not improve much," a second trend said.
Traders said low physical prices would also prevent the futures contracts to rise further.
Physical copper is around 22,900 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, down from last week's 23,100 yuan, traders said.
Aluminium ended down. June fell 60 to 14,850, July fell 50 to 14,900, August 20 to 15,100 and September 150 to 15,150.
Combined volume fell to 1,290 tonnes from 2,240 tonnes.
